title: Joining the GATE Project Team to Advance AI Governance
summary: Joined the GATE Project Team, contributing to interdisciplinary research on AI governance, responsible AI and the societal implications of emerging technologies.
body:
I joined the GATE Project Team, contributing to interdisciplinary research exploring the governance of emerging technologies and the responsible development and use of artificial intelligence.

The collaboration brings together perspectives on AI governance, responsible AI, technology policy and the societal implications of emerging technologies. It provides an opportunity to contribute to research addressing how AI can be developed and deployed in ways that are responsible, trustworthy and aligned with the needs of society.

Joining the GATE Project Team expands my work beyond the application of AI in health and education towards the broader questions of how AI should be governed, how responsibility can be designed into AI systems, and how emerging technologies can serve society.
seoTitle: Yao Xie Joins GATE Project Team to Advance AI Governance
metaDescription: Yao Xie joins the GATE Project Team, contributing to interdisciplinary research on AI governance, responsible AI, technology policy and the societal implications of emerging technologies.

title: New Preprint Examines Digital and AI-Enabled Healthcare Professions Education in LMICs
summary: A new systematic review protocol examines how digital technologies and AI are used in healthcare professions education across low- and middle-income countries.
body:
A new systematic review protocol, “Digital and Artificial Intelligence Enabled Healthcare Professions Education in Low- and Middle-Income Countries,” has been released as a preprint.

The study examines how digital technologies and artificial intelligence are being used in healthcare professions education across low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). It aims to map the available evidence and identify how AI-enabled and digitally supported approaches may contribute to the education and development of future healthcare professionals.

The research sits at the intersection of artificial intelligence, health professions education, global health and equity, reflecting an ongoing interest in how emerging technologies can be applied responsibly across different educational and healthcare contexts.

Authors: Yao Xie, Kayode Philip Fadahunsi, John O'Donoghue.
seoTitle: AI-Enabled Healthcare Education in Low- and Middle-Income Countries | Yao Xie
metaDescription: New systematic review protocol examines digital and AI-enabled healthcare professions education in low- and middle-income countries.

title: Developing a Capability Framework for Sustainable Well-being
summary: A new preprint develops a capability framework for sustainable well-being through an international modified e-Delphi study.
body:
A new preprint, “Well-being Efficacy: Developing a Capability Framework for Sustainable Well-being through an International Modified e-Delphi Study,” has been released.

The study develops a capability framework for sustainable well-being through an international modified e-Delphi process, bringing together perspectives from researchers and professionals across multiple disciplines.

The research explores the capabilities that may enable individuals and communities to develop greater agency, knowledge and capacity to sustain well-being. It contributes to an emerging research agenda around well-being efficacy, human capability and sustainable well-being.

Authors: Yao Xie, Kayode Philip Fadahunsi, Nandakumar Ravichandran, Nia Clendennen, Sheila Loughman, John Broughan, Brian O'Mahony, Geoff McCombe, John O'Donoghue, Joseph Gallagher et al.
seoTitle: Well-being Efficacy: A Capability Framework for Sustainable Well-being
metaDescription: International research develops a capability framework for sustainable well-being through a modified e-Delphi study.

title: New Research on Long COVID and General Practice in Ireland
summary: Research examining Long COVID and general practice in the Republic of Ireland has been published in the Irish Journal of Medical Science.
body:
Research examining Long COVID and general practice in the Republic of Ireland has been published in the Irish Journal of Medical Science.

The study, “Long covid and general practice: a survey of patients in the Republic of Ireland,” provides evidence on patients’ experiences of Long COVID and their interactions with primary care.

The research contributes to a broader understanding of Long COVID, primary care and patient experience in Ireland, and highlights the importance of evidence-informed approaches to supporting people living with persistent health conditions.

Authors: John Broughan, Yao Xie, Crea Carberry, Sarah O'Connell, Jacinta Fay, Pamela Morrison, Nandakumar Ravichandran, Stefano Savinelli, Geoff McCombe, Mary Higgins et al.
seoTitle: Long COVID and General Practice in Ireland | Research by Yao Xie
metaDescription: Research published in the Irish Journal of Medical Science examines patient experiences of Long COVID and general practice in Ireland.

title: Bringing Research into the Real World at Hult Prize Ireland 2026
summary: Took part in the Hult Prize Ireland National Competition, marking a step from academic research towards real-world innovation and entrepreneurship.
body:
In April 2026, I took part in the Hult Prize Ireland National Competition, marking an important step in my journey from academic research towards real-world innovation.

For the first time, I brought ideas emerging from my research out of the academic environment and into a real-world entrepreneurial setting, where they had to be communicated, challenged and considered in terms of practical value and impact.

The experience was an opportunity to test what happens when research meets the realities of users, problems, implementation, entrepreneurship and the wider innovation ecosystem.

More than simply a competition, it became a valuable learning experience in research translation, turning academic ideas into something that can be understood, questioned and potentially applied beyond academia.

The 2026 Ireland National Competition brought together student-led teams from universities across Ireland to compete on a national stage.
